flawed_step: Any proof attempt fails at the step that would go from 3-connected claw-free to Hamiltonian. Nothing in these hypotheses forces a Hamiltonian cycle. Replacing each vertex of a non-Hamiltonian 3-connected cubic graph with a triangle keeps the graph claw-free and 3-connected, but the new graph is still not Hamiltonian. (The Matthews–Sumner conjecture needs 4-connectivity.)
counterexample:
Start with the Petersen graph P. Its vertices are 0..9. Outer 5-cycle: 0-1-2-3-4-0. Inner pentagram: 5-7-9-6-8-5. Spokes: i-(i+5) for i=0..4. P is cubic, 3-edge-connected and non-Hamiltonian.

Build H by replacing each vertex of P with a triangle. H has 30 vertices (v,e), one for each vertex v of P and each edge e of P at v. Edges of H:
(a) (v,e)-(v,f) for e≠f, so each vertex v gives a triangle T_v;
(b) (u,e)-(v,e) for each edge e=uv of P, a perfect matching.

1. Claw-free: each vertex of H has exactly 3 neighbours: its two triangle-mates, which are adjacent to each other, and its matching partner. Any 3 neighbours include that adjacent pair, so no induced K_{1,3} exists.

2. 3-connected: H has 30 ≥ 4 vertices. Delete any set S with |S| ≤ 2.
- No triangle is removed completely, and what is left of each T_v is still connected.
- Each deleted vertex disables at most one matching edge, so at most 2 edges of P are disabled.
- P minus 2 edges is still connected, because P is 3-edge-connected.
- So the leftover triangle pieces stay linked through the remaining matching edges, and H−S is connected.

3. Not Hamiltonian: suppose C is a Hamiltonian cycle of H.
- C must leave and re-enter each T_v. Only 3 edges leave T_v, and a cycle crosses any cut an even number of times, so C uses exactly 2 of them.
- The matching edges used by C therefore form a spanning 2-regular subgraph F of P.
- Contracting each triangle turns C into a closed walk that follows F, so F is connected.
- A connected spanning 2-regular subgraph of P would be a Hamiltonian cycle of P. P has none, which is a contradiction.

So H is a 3-connected claw-free graph with no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The counterexample is the Petersen graph with each vertex replaced by a triangle (30 vertices, cubic). It is claw-free because every vertex's neighbourhood contains an edge. It is 3-connected because deleting 2 vertices never removes a whole triangle and cuts at most 2 edges of the 3-edge-connected Petersen graph. It is not Hamiltonian because a Hamiltonian cycle would use exactly 2 of the 3 edges leaving each triangle, which would give a Hamiltonian cycle of the Petersen graph, and that graph has none.
